items.problem: First full build failed with 5x 'CS0103: The name \'App\' does not exist in the current context' across MainPage.xaml.cs and Scenario1_DataEvents.xaml.cs.
items.evidence: session-log.txt lines 2360-2364 (build errors); fixed turn 31 by adding 'using RelativeInclinometer;'. Confirmed: App.xaml.cs is 'namespace RelativeInclinometer;' (x:Class RelativeInclinometer.App) while MainPage.xaml.cs / SampleConfiguration.cs are 'namespace SDKTemplate'.
items.skill_search: Grepped SKILL.md, MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md, scripts/* for 'SDKTemplate', 'CS0103', 'RootNamespace', 'App class' — zero hits.
items.root_cause: Windows-universal-samples put shared scaffolding (App refs, MainPage, SampleConfiguration/Scenario) in 'namespace SDKTemplate', but 'dotnet new winui' scaffolds the App class in the project ROOT namespace. The namespace split leaves every unqualified 'App.*' reference in the SDKTemplate files unresolved.
items.proposed_fix: Add a 'CS0103: The name App does not exist (SDKTemplate namespace split)' entry to MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md 'Common build errors after the namespace rewrite', giving both fixes: (A) add 'using <RootNamespace>;' to SDKTemplate files, or (B, preferred for many refs) move the scaffold App into 'namespace SDKTemplate' (App.xaml x:Class + App.xaml.cs).
items.generalizes: Nearly every UWP app in these scenarios derives from Windows-universal-samples, which universally use the 'namespace SDKTemplate' convention while the WinUI 3 scaffold uses the project root namespace. This CS0103 App failure will recur on essentially every SDK-sample migration.
